diagnosis.root_cause: CRM marks customer 19426 inactive, but the RADIUS record remains provisioned without the required suspension or Framed-Pool restriction. The customer is therefore still authenticated, assigned 10.5.50.188 from pool_Users, and passing traffic.
evidence: The ONU is online and responding, with RX -22.44 dBm and TX 2.36 dBm, both within healthy EPON ranges.
The seven-day optical telemetry is stable: RX remains around -22 dBm, TX remains around +2.3 dBm, distance is constant at 178, and TX bias current stays within the healthy range.
All tested peer ONUs on EPON0/4 are online and healthy, so there is no customer-specific optical outage, splitter failure, or PON-port failure.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, its metrics are near baseline, and all eight PONs are healthy; the router heartbeat is also healthy.
The customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as VLAN 1014, so this is not a VLAN 46 or stuck-provisioning fault.
The RADIUS record exists and maps to the correct line ID, ruling out a missing-entry or line-ID-conflict fault.
CRM reports the subscriber as inactive, while RADIUS has no Framed-Pool suspension applied; the customer has an active address in 10.5.50.188 and recorded traffic.
The session count is normal at two sessions in 24 hours with long durations, so there is no session-flapping fault.
The direct CRM/RADIUS inconsistency identifies a suspended subscriber who is still being served.

remediation.action: Synchronize the CRM suspension to RADIUS by applying the appropriate suspended-service policy or removing/disabling the active RADIUS authorization, terminate the current session, and verify that subsequent authentication is rejected or placed in the suspension pool. Confirm that the customer remains inactive in CRM and that no unintended service or traffic persists.

ground_truth.root_cause: The customer is marked inactive in CRM but RADIUS never applied the suspension. Framed-Pool is unset and the assigned address is in pool_Users, so full service continues. This is one of the 218 such cases in the estate.
expected_reasoning: CRM marks the customer inactive, which should mean service is suspended
RADIUS has a radcheck row with no Framed-Pool set
A suspended customer should be assigned to pool_Disable_Users and hold an address in 10.200.200.0/24
The assigned address is 10.5.50.188, which is in pool_Users, the standard subscriber range
The IP range settles the question without relying on either system's status flag
Sessions are active with a 715 minute mean and traffic is normal across all seven days
The customer is therefore receiving full service despite being suspended in CRM
The optical layer is healthy and irrelevant to this fault
There is no service impact for the customer; the impact is commercial
distractors: Every technical signal is healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
No customer has complained and none will
service_impact is false even though a genuine fault exists
